title: Test Types
concept:
A **test type** is a group of test activities focused on specific test objectives. Whereas a test *level* tells you what stage of development you're at, a test *type* tells you what quality characteristic you're exercising. The four main test types apply at every test level.

**Functional testing** evaluates what the system does — does it implement the required functions correctly? Derived from functional requirements; can use black-box techniques.

**Non-functional testing** evaluates how well the system performs its functions — performance, usability, reliability, security, compatibility, portability, maintainability (the ISO 25010 quality characteristics minus functional suitability). Often requires specialised tools (load generators, security scanners).

**Black-box (specification-based) testing** derives tests from the specification of the test object without reference to its internal structure. Both functional and non-functional tests can be black-box.

**White-box (structure-based) testing** derives tests from the internal structure of the test object — control flow, data flow, code. Typical at component level: statement coverage, branch coverage.

A single test can combine types: a load test (non-functional) using functional scenarios (functional) executed against a system whose internal structure is unknown (black-box).
keyPoints: Four test types: functional, non-functional, black-box (specification-based), white-box (structure-based).
Types apply at every test level — you can do functional, non-functional, black-box, and white-box at component, integration, system, and acceptance levels.
Test types are based on objectives; types and levels are independent dimensions.

quiz.question: A tester verifies that a checkout page loads in under 2 seconds with 1000 concurrent users. Which test types is this BEST classified as?
quiz.explanation: Response time under load is a performance characteristic — non-functional. The tester does not need access to the internal code to apply load and measure response time — black-box.
